name: VAST Data
summary: VAST Data provides a data platform for AI, analytics, and enterprise workloads across large-scale infrastructure.
overview: VAST Data builds a distributed data platform designed for AI-era data and compute workloads.
bull_case: AI pushes data architecture from a storage purchase into a strategic system of record for model and agent workloads.
bear_case: Cloud providers and storage incumbents can compete aggressively, and the valuation relies on sustained high growth.
directory_notes: Valuation more than tripled from a $9.1B Series E in 2023, per company.
AI data-platform adoption, profitability, and cloud competition.

intelligence.description: VAST Data sells a unified data platform for AI and analytics workloads. Its bet is that enterprises need a new data architecture as models, agents, and high-performance compute make older storage silos less useful.
company: VAST Data was founded in 2016 to rethink distributed data systems for modern compute. It markets a platform that unifies storage, databases, and data-management services for high-performance AI and enterprise workloads.

The company said its April 2026 Series F reflected a combination of growth and profitability. The funding, led by Drive Capital with Access Industries as co-lead, more than tripled the valuation assigned to its 2023 Series E.
intelligence.why_it_matters: AI systems depend on accessible, governed, high-throughput data. VAST is a private-market signal for whether the infrastructure layer beneath models can capture a large share of the economics, rather than becoming a commodity owned by hyperscalers.

changed.text: Raised a Series D as the company expanded enterprise data-platform adoption.
Announced a Series F at $30B, describing a rare combination of growth and profitability.

takeaways: VAST is selling architecture, not simply storage capacity.
Its tripled valuation reflects the expectation that AI creates a durable need for high-performance data platforms.
Reported profitability makes the growth narrative more credible than a purely capital-funded build-out.
Hyperscalers, incumbent storage vendors, and the pace of enterprise AI deployment are the main risks.
